name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean of roughly 22 points
Incumbent Mike Bost running with a massive cash advantage ($846K vs $34K)
Prediction markets price a Democratic upset at about 1%
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending indicate competition
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a deeply Republican district, a renominated incumbent who has out-raised his challenger roughly ten to one, and markets that see almost no chance of an upset. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving off a Safe Republican rating.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Bost or a dramatic national wave against his party would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southern Illinois' 12th District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward the GOP. Mike Bost, the incumbent representative, has been renominated and seeks another term against Democrat Julie Fortier, a first-time challenger with minimal financial backing.

The fundamentals strongly favor Bost. He has raised about $1.6 million and holds roughly $846,000 on hand, compared with about $34,000 for Fortier, and no outside spending has targeted the race. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 1% chance of an upset, and no public polls or expert ratings signal competitiveness. The forecast rates the district as Safe Republican, with Bost expected to win by a wide margin in November.
